subject: physics_2

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: ionization is the removal of an atomic electron by the Coulomb force of the passing particle. A neutron has zero charge, so it has essentially no direct ionizing power; the small ionization observed with neutron beams is INDIRECT, from the recoil protons and reaction products they create. The book states only the direct part.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Ionization needs an electric force
steps.mark_note: A neutral particle exerts no force on electrons
lines: To ionize an atom, a particle must pull an
electron out of it. That needs an electric
force between the particle and the electron.
A neutron is uncharged, so it exerts no such
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the electric force that a neutral particle cannot exert.
steps.why: Ionizing power comes from the Coulomb pull or push of a charged particle as it passes an atom; a neutral particle passes without any such interaction with the electrons.
common_mistakes: Saying the neutron is too slow. Speed is not the reason; charge is.
Saying the neutron never interacts. It does interact, but with nuclei, not electrons.

recall.must_convey: That ionization needs an electric force on the atomic electrons, and a neutron is uncharged so it exerts none.
accept: no electric force on the electrons
reject: alpha and beta have high ionizing power

steps.memory_tip: No charge, no pull on the electrons, no ionization.

steps.label: Very low ionizing power

A neutron loses its energy by colliding with
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The comparison with α and β carries this half.
steps.why: Because it cannot ionize, a neutron travels a long way through matter before it is stopped — the same fact that makes it highly penetrating makes it a poor ioniser.
common_mistakes: Saying the ionizing power is exactly zero. It is very small, and any ionization is indirect.
Leaving out α and β. The question expects the comparison.

recall.must_convey: That the ionizing power of a neutron is very small compared with alpha and beta particles, and it loses energy by colliding with nuclei.
accept: ionizing power is very less than alpha and beta
loses energy by collision with nuclei

steps.memory_tip: Poor ioniser, deep traveller — the same missing charge explains both.

insider_note: Two marks: the missing electric force, then the comparison with α-particles and β-particles.
